components.name: Theme
components.summary: An app's colours for light and dark, installed once, and the gradient pairs the derived square picks from. Nothing draws a colour it did not ask the theme for.

at: Theme.kt: the app's MaterialTheme and Palette
how: The app's theme wraps the root in MaterialTheme(colorScheme for dark or light); read colours from MaterialTheme.colorScheme.
Space.xs … Space.xl, Space.corner: the spacing scale every screen uses.
ArkTheme(art) carries the derived square's pairs; an app hands it its own, as the desktop installs its palette.
Space.* for spacing; the system's colours, with the app's colour as the accent.
Squares holds the derived square's pairs.

components.name: Style
components.summary: Text tones, buttons, scrollbars, grounds and surfaces, and the rows a cursor lights.

how: Material 3's roles: onSurfaceVariant for a dim line, primary for the accent.
The typography sets names and headings in bold, as on the desktop.
.foregroundStyle(.secondary) for a dim line, .tint for the accent.

how: maxLines = 1 and overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis cut the end; the platform has no middle cut.
.lineLimit(1) and .truncationMode(.middle) for a name, .tail for a heading.

how: Square(seed, modifier)
Cover(seed, art, side, modifier, round = false, corner = Space.corner): the square until the picture loads.
Art.hash is FNV-1a over UTF-16, the desktop's.

components.name: Navigation
components.summary: Where the places are: a sidebar on the desktop, a tab bar on a phone. The one under the cursor, or the tab that is lit, is the page.

at: the app's Chrome: the tab bar and the mini player
how: Chrome(tab, player, controls, onTab) { page }: the tab bar and the mini player around a page.
TabStack keeps each tab's page alive; tapping the lit tab again is Reselect.
Shell is a TabView, Home, Library and Search, each tab its own NavigationStack; the mini player is its tabViewBottomAccessory.
.tabBarMinimizeBehavior(.onScrollDown): the bar shrinks as a page scrolls.

ListRow(onClick, title, under, trailing = { Chevron() }) { picture }
TrackNumber(n, playing) is the leading slot on an album's page.
TrackRow(track:under:from:onPlay:)
Its context menu is TrackActions, the same entries as Android's sheet.

A shelf is a LazyRow of them, side from the screen's width.

components.name: Keys
components.summary: The keyboard grammar and the grids it moves a cursor over. j and k walk this page's sidebar.

components.name: Waking
components.summary: What wakes a window that runs no loop, and what holds the splash until the first screen is ready.

how: holdSplashUntil(ceilingMs) { ready }: in onCreate, before setContent.

entries.name: Theme
entries.summary: An app's palette, installed once: light and dark iced palettes and the derived square's gradient pairs for each. Every style closure asks `of(theme)` rather than writing a colour down, which is why dark mode works.
rules: Install before the first frame; a second install is refused, so one window has one answer to "what colour is this".
NEUTRAL (AppKit greys, system blue) is the only colour arkui owns. This page draws with it.

entries.name: Style
entries.summary: The style closures every widget is handed: text tones, buttons, scrollbars, the page's ground and the surface a step off it, hairlines, and the rows a cursor lights.
rules: A scrollbar is never the accent.
A row under the cursor is marked whether or not its pane has the keys, and lit only while it has.

entries.name: Glyphs
entries.summary: The table of Lucide drawings, as SVG bytes. `LICENSE.lucide` sits beside it.
api: ADD_TO, ALBUM, ARTIST, BACK, CHEVRON, CLOSE, COMPOSER, DEBUG, DEVICES, DOWN, HOME, LAPTOP, LIBRARY, MINUS, MORE, MUTED, NEXT, NOTE, OFFLINE, ONLINE, PAUSE, PHONE, PLAY, PLAYING, PLAYLIST, PLUS, PREVIOUS, PULPIT, SEARCH, SHOW, SHUFFLE, SIGN_OUT, SKIP_BACK, SKIP_FORWARD, SPEAKER, STOP, TICK, TICKED, UNTICK, VOLUME
rules: Drawn with currentColor; the colour is the icon's tint, never the file's.

entries.name: Icon
entries.summary: A glyph drawn at a size in a colour asked of the palette. The named ones are the tones a row, a panel or a control needs.
rules: The colour goes through the svg style filter, so one drawing serves every tone.

entries.name: Format
entries.summary: Words for numbers: a clock, a count spelt out, a plural, a span of time, a day.
rules: A length past an hour is h:mm:ss.

entries.name: Fit
entries.summary: Cutting text to a width: from the end or through the middle, measured in pixels, and the characters the typeface cannot draw spelt in ones it can.
rules: A name loses its middle, a heading its end.

entries.name: URL
entries.summary: Percent-encoding for a fragment, so a `/`, a `#` or an accent survives the address bar.

entries.name: Sidebar
entries.summary: A column of places down the left of a window, grouped under headings; the one under the cursor is the page beside it. This page's own sidebar is one.
api: Item { glyph, label, heading, count, press }
view(items, cursor, focused, width, padding, id)
rules: One highlight, not two: the cursor is what the page shows, marked always, lit only while the sidebar has the keys.
A heading is drawn where the group changes, not stored as a row, so row n is the cursor's n.
Its pixel of edge is part of its width.

entries.name: Panel
entries.summary: The shape every context window is: a bordered panel, a title, and fixed-height entries with a glyph column that is there whether or not it has a glyph.
api: PADDING, ENTRY, TITLE, ENTRY_CHAR, ENTRY_CHROME, EDGE, RADIUS
rules: Heights are declared constants: a panel is placed before iced lays it out.

entries.name: Table
entries.summary: Rows of cells cut to their columns at layout, headings over them, section labels and the transport's gutter.
rules: A cell loses its middle and a heading its end, each to its own column.
Columns are portions, so no text column pushes another off a narrow window.

entries.name: Line
entries.summary: One line of text cut, at layout, to the width it is given; `gives_way` lays it out after the rest of its row.
rules: A row lays out in order, so a line first in it would take everything; giving way puts it last.

entries.name: Cards
entries.summary: A grid of pictures with a name and a line under each, the arithmetic of how many fit, and a page's header of picture, name and facts.
api: Card { seed, title, under, round, picture, open }
view(shelf, cards, pane, cursor, empty, on_hover, scroll, on_scroll)
header(picture, kind, name, under, open_under, facts, padding)
rules: A person is a circle and a record a square.
The keyboard and the view divide the same pane width, so `l` lands where it looks.

entries.name: Hero
entries.summary: The wide banner a page can open with, the bold face, section headings, and a listing of entries in columns with a "more" after them.
api: Entry { over, title, under, count, open }
rules: Fira Sans Bold is embedded: a browser has no system fonts, and with none bold is not bold.

entries.name: Art
entries.summary: The derived square: a gradient picked from a name, the same on every device, and the real picture over it once it arrives.
rules: The hash is the phones' too, so a name has one square everywhere.

entries.name: Account
entries.summary: Who is signed in as a circle — their picture, or initials on a colour picked from their name — and the menu that hangs off it.
rules: Nobody goes offline by hand: the menu signs out, and nothing else.

entries.name: Menu
entries.summary: The dropdown: a title and entries, as wide as its longest entry, opened at the pointer or lined up under a control, with submenus beside it. The theme control at the top of this page is one.
rules: A right click opens at the pointer; a control's menu opens at the control.
As wide as its longest entry, within 198..=420: AppKit's rule.
A submenu laps the parent by exactly its padding, so the lit row touches its edge.
A submenu opens after a 200ms rest, not on the way past.

entries.name: Picker
entries.summary: A list of choices each ticked or not, with an optional last row that names a new one — on its own in the middle, or as a menu's submenu.
api: view(picker, focused, Messages { at, activate, name, create })
rules: A submenu draws no header: the menu it hangs off is still up with the title.

entries.name: Context
entries.summary: A menu, its submenu, or a picker alone, and the rules for them together: which one has the keys, the dwell, `l` in and `h` out, `<Esc>`.
rules: Closing a menu takes its submenu with it.
An app refuses its rows' hover while a layer is up: a backdrop cannot swallow a hover.

entries.name: Layer
entries.summary: What goes under and around an overlay: a backdrop that closes on a click and swallows the wheel, a dimmed one, and pinned or centred placement.
rules: A submenu gets no backdrop of its own: a second one over the menu would eat its clicks.

entries.name: Dialog
entries.summary: A titled window rising over a page as the page dims.
api: view(title, close, body, width, height, open)
rules: `open` is eased; ask `opening` whether to keep a clock running.

entries.name: Keys
entries.summary: The keyboard grammar — counts, gg/G, ^d/^u, / and n/N, <Tab>, <Esc> — and the grids it moves a cursor over. j and k move this page's sidebar.
api: Keys::new(), press(key, mods) -> Option<Action>, pending(), mode()
Action::{Move, Activate, Toggle, Search, Match, Cycle, Cancel, Jump, Key}
Motion::{Down, Up, Left, Right, First, Last, To}
Grid { cells, columns }, column, row, step, progress
rules: `step` returns None only at that edge, which means "not mine": the app says what lies past it.

entries.name: Route
entries.summary: Places as URL fragments, and the address bar kept in step: reconciled, not pushed, and a scrub one history entry. Each page here has one.
api: Router::new(), sync(&place), replace_next(), poll(ready), go(by), can_go(by)
rules: `parse` never fails: an unknown fragment is home.
Call `sync` after every update.

entries.name: Scroll
entries.summary: Keeping a keyboard cursor on screen.

entries.name: Swipe
entries.summary: Two fingers sideways as back and forward, with the arrow drawn over the page as they go.
api: Swipe::feed, tick, allow, active, offset, arrow
rules: It goes when the fingers lift, and only where there is somewhere to go.
In a browser the browser's own back does this instead.

entries.name: Wake
entries.summary: What wakes a window that runs no loop: a bell anything can ring, one timer at a deadline, and the browser's address bar moving.
rules: With nothing playing, dwelling or arriving, a window runs no timer.

entries.name: Images
entries.summary: A picture cache: fetched off the render thread, decoded and bounded, kept on disk natively and in the Cache API in a browser. A failure is remembered.
rules: The renderer is handed pixels at the size they are drawn, not a megapixel JPEG to decode inside a frame.
